newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries open lower, focus on 10-yr auction.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries open lower, focus on 10-yr auction.

text.p: U.S. government securities prices opened modestly lower on Wednesday as participants adjusted positions before the Treasury's 10-year note auction.
The Treasury will sell $12.0 billion in 10-year notes this afternoon in the second leg of its three-part quarterly refunding operation.
The bidding deadline for the notes is 1300 EDT/1700 GMT.
The Treasury sold $16.0 billion in three-year notes on Tuesday and it is scheduled to sell $10.0 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was down 4/32 to 101-20/32, yielding 6.50 percent, in early dealings.
"Obviously, the 10-year auction is the focus for the market and it should keep us under pressure at least until the afternoon," said David Shabelman, Treasury market analyst at Standard & Poor's MMS.
Shabelman said some people believe that the 10-year auction will be the most significant part of the Treasury's quarterly refunding.
"It will probably gauge interest in securities that are farther out on the maturity curve," he said.
"It could go a ways to determining how tomorrow's (30-year Treasury bond) auction will go as well," he said.
Shabelman called the support that the 30-year bond yield has drawn at 6.50 percent was notable.

"It's been pretty impressive that support has held at 6.50 percent because there have been reasons for (the yield) to go above there," he said. "We had the huge move (down) on Friday and we haven't seen much more of a breakdown in front of all this (Treasury refunding) supply."
Shabelman said if the 30-year bond yield were to move above 6.50 percent and stays there for "any appreciable amount of time," it could cause some more longs to liquidate.
Analysts said the Beige Book release by the Federal Reserve at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT would get attention but was unlikely to offer any observations not already familiar to market participants.
"You'll hear a lot of the same things from the Fed that you have been hearing," said Shabelman. "There shouldn't be much that's too threatening in that."

The next key piece of economic data for the market is the July retail sales report, due next Wednesday. Financial market participants are interested in that data because they want information on how aggressively consumers will spend in the third quarter after cutting back in the second.
Trading on a when-issued basis, the 10-year notes being auctioned today yielded 6.2175 percent.
The 30-year bonds to be sold on Thursday were yielding 6.4675 percent.
The two-year Treasury note was unchanged at 99-29/32 to yield 5.93 percent.
The five-year note was down 1/32 to 99-14/32 to yield 6.13 percent.
Ten-year notes were down 2/32 at 102-24/32 to yield 6.24 percent.
Three- , six- and year bill rates were all unchanged at 5.15 percent, 5.21 percent and 5.24 percent, respectively. (( -- North American Treasury Desk, 212-859-1679 ))
